quizzes.stem: A PreToolUse hook is meant to rewrite a command before it runs. It returns the new input in a field next to `hookSpecificOutput`, and the original command runs unchanged. What is the cause?

options.a: The value is honoured only when nested in the answer structure
options.b: A rewrite takes effect only if the hook answers with a deferral
options.c: Commands can be rewritten only by a hook that runs as a separate program
options.d: The rewrite was applied, then undone by the session's permission mode

explanation.a: The answer is read only from its documented place.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a deferral discards the change: "the input is dropped".
explanation.c: Ruled out because callback hooks may change input too: "Pair `updatedInput` with `permissionDecision: 'allow'` to auto-approve the modified input".
explanation.d: Ruled out because nothing undoes a change that is applied: "the modified input still applies and flows through the normal permission evaluation".

quizzes.stem: A team adds a hook with the matcher `src/payments/*` to review every write under that folder. The hook never fires. What is the best fix?

options.a: Switch the matcher to a regular expression that also lists every file in the folder
options.b: Correct the spelling of the event key, since event names are case-sensitive
options.c: Attach it to the file-editing tools and test the path inside the callback
options.d: Move the hook to the PostToolUse event, which evaluates paths after the write

explanation.c: A matcher sees only the name of the tool, so the path is read from the input.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Matchers only match tool names, not file paths or other arguments."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the event key is not at fault here, the matcher is: "the matcher must match the tool name exactly".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a post hook's matcher is read the same way: "For tool events it is tested against the tool name".

quizzes.stem: A support agent uses three vendor systems: one gives epoch seconds, one a numeric status code, one local date text. The model keeps comparing dates wrongly. Which fix fits best, given that the team does not own them?

options.a: A longer system prompt that teaches the model each vendor's date format by example
options.b: A PostToolUse hook that supplies one readable format as the replacement output
options.c: A prompt-based hook that judges each result and rewrites the dates it finds wrong
options.d: A larger model for the support agent, so that it converts each format correctly

explanation.b: The hook converts once, in code, for any tool, before the model reads the result.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a conversion in the model's head can be wrong, and the page assigns that task to code: "is a prompt for a task with a right answer".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a model judging each result keeps the conversion probabilistic and "gives up the point of determinism".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a larger model still converts by reasoning, and "a conversion done in the model's head is a conversion that can be wrong".

quizzes.stem: A team commits a git-push guard to the project's `.claude/settings.json`. Its batch service runs the SDK with `setting_sources=[]` and a callback hook for refunds. A push attempt from the service is not blocked. Why?

options.a: The callback hook overrides every command hook that the settings define
options.b: Command hooks are meant for interactive sessions of Claude Code only
options.c: The guard is in the project file, but the service reads the user file
options.d: Nothing reads the shared checked-in settings file in that deployment

explanation.d: With no setting sources the SDK collects only the callbacks.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the two kinds run side by side: "next to its callbacks, in parallel and with the most restrictive answer applying".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the SDK collects "shell command hooks from settings files when the corresponding `setting_sources` entry is enabled".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the user's file is skipped as well: the service "ignores the command hooks of every settings file".

quizzes.stem: A team checks the refund limit in a PostToolUse hook and, when a refund is above the limit, the hook exits with code 2. Large refunds still happen. What is the cause, and the fix?

options.a: Exit 2 does not block in the SDK, so the hook must return a denial
options.b: Post hooks may not fire at all, so the limit needs a much longer timeout
options.c: The money has moved by then, so the control belongs ahead of the call
options.d: The hook gave no replacement result, so it must return a corrected output

explanation.c: A post hook runs after the effect.
explanation.a: Ruled out because exit 2 reports back and cannot stop what has run: for `PostToolUse` it "Shows stderr to Claude; the tool already ran".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the turn-limit case is a different one: "Hooks may not fire when the agent hits the `max_turns` limit because the session ends before hooks can execute".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a corrected output changes only what the model reads, not the effect: "The refund exists whatever the model is shown."

quizzes.stem: On Claude Code v2.1.210 or later, a PreToolUse gate in the SDK waits on a slow vendor lookup and exceeds its time limit. What does the model receive, and is the action carried out?

options.a: A normal tool result, since a silent hook counts as raising no objection
options.b: A notice that the hook never replied by its deadline, and the operation is withheld
options.c: A rejection from a person, and the whole run stops until someone responds to it
options.d: Nothing at all, and the turn simply waits until the gate finally gives its answer

explanation.b: A timed-out gate is the safe case: nothing runs and the model is told.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the tool is not run: "Claude Code doesn't run the tool call".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the model gets a result and the turn goes on: "Claude receives a tool result stating the hook didn't respond before its timeout".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a callback past its timeout is stopped: "Claude Code cancels it and discards its output".

quizzes.stem: A second callback was written to use the corrected input that a first callback produces, and it sometimes sees the original. What is the right design?

options.a: Register the first one earlier so that it always runs before the other
options.b: Add a delay to the second one so that the first has time to finish
options.c: Return the corrected input from both, so that the last one applies
options.d: Merge both steps into one function, so that the order no longer matters

explanation.a: Ruled out because the order of registration does not set the order of completion: "all matching hooks run in parallel".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a delay still chains the two callbacks, and "Two hooks cannot be a pipeline."
explanation.c: Ruled out because there is no fixed last one: "completion order is non-deterministic".
